source: What happened? Both approaches produce the same output, but notice the difference. Without a loop, you need three separate print statements. With a loop, you write the print statement once and it runs three times. The loop version is shorter, easier to read, and if you wanted to count to 100, you'd just change range(1, 4) to range(1, 101) instead of writing 100 print statements! This is the power of loops.
